skill.name: git-workflow
skill.description: Git best practices for commits, branches, pull requests, and collaboration workflows following Conventional Commits and GitFlow patterns
skill.summary: Apply consistent Git conventions for commits, branches, reviews, releases, and team collaboration.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent commits and branches make collaboration and releases harder to manage. This skill applies Conventional Commits, GitFlow, review practices, and pre-commit checks.
actual_capabilities: Formats commit messages with Conventional Commit types, scopes, and concise subjects.
Suggests branch names using work type, ticket identifier, and short description.
Explains GitFlow paths for features, releases, and hotfixes.
Provides local checks for staged secrets, linting, type checking, and tests.
Guides pull request preparation, collaboration, and code review practices.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples rather than an automated Git integration.
It does not replace repository-specific contribution or release policies.
Its secret check uses simple pattern matching and cannot detect every credential.
It does not cover advanced recovery, rebasing, signing, or repository administration.

use_cases.title: Prepare Clean Contributions
use_cases.description: Create consistent commits and branches before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Team Releases
use_cases.description: Map feature, release, and hotfix branches through a shared GitFlow process.

use_cases.title: Teach Repository Conventions
use_cases.description: Give contributors clear examples for commit messages, branch names, and pre-commit checks.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Conventional Commit message for these changes: [describe changes]. Include an appropriate type, optional scope, and concise subject.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after completing a focused change.

prompt_templates.title: Name a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a branch name for ticket [ID] about [work]. Choose feature, bugfix, or hotfix and use a short lowercase description.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a GitFlow release for version [version], including branch sources, merge targets, review points, and pre-commit quality checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when coordinating a scheduled release.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Team Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Git workflow: [workflow details]. Identify history, collaboration, release, and secret-handling risks, then propose a safer sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when improving an established repository process.

output_examples.input: We added OAuth2 login support in the authentication module.
output_examples.output: Recommended commit: feat(auth): add OAuth2 login support. This uses the feature type and identifies the authentication scope.

output_examples.input: Create a branch for ticket CORE-456, which fixes a null pointer.
output_examples.output: Recommended branch: bugfix/CORE-456-fix-null-pointer. The bugfix prefix distinguishes corrective work from features and production hotfixes.

output_examples.input: How should a production security hotfix move through GitFlow?
output_examples.output: Branch from main, review and validate the fix, then merge it into both main and develop. Run repository quality checks before merging.

best_practices: Keep each commit focused and use a clear Conventional Commit type.
Follow repository-specific branch protections and review requirements.
Inspect staged changes for secrets and run all configured quality checks.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated changes in one commit.
Do not bypass reviews or protected branch rules for routine work.
Do not treat a simple secret search as complete credential scanning.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command examples for an agent or user to apply.

faq.question: Which commit convention does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Conventional Commits with a type, optional scope, and concise subject.

faq.question: Which branch model does it describe?
faq.answer: It describes GitFlow with main, develop, feature, release, and hotfix branches.

faq.question: Can it detect every staged secret?
faq.answer: No. Its example search catches common names but cannot replace dedicated secret-scanning tools.

faq.question: Will it adapt to repository rules?
faq.answer: Provide the repository policy in your prompt, because local contribution rules should take priority.
